title: The Telegram ban order misses the tech-law nuance
description: The Delhi High Court's decision in Telegram FZ LLC v. Union of India is important not only because it concerns the temporary blocking of one of the world's largest messaging platforms in India, but also because it tests a basic question of statutory architecture under the Information Technology Act, 2000.Section 69A is usually discussed as a censorship provision, a national security provision, or a public order provision. In this case, the more important question is narrower and more technical:
